text: The app stores its data in one SQLite file in the user's data folder, with no server (D1, `@decided`). It runs on Node.js 24 with no runtime dependencies (D5, `@decided`). Sync between machines is not decided (D3, `@open`), and that decision waits for the user.

Export uses CSV, one row per note (D2, `@decided`). The maximum length of a note is 2000 characters (D4, `@decided`), so a row holds at most that much note text. Sync between machines is still `@open` (D3) and waits for the user.

The maximum length of a note is 2000 characters (D4, `@decided`). The spec does not say whether the limit counts characters or bytes, so tell me if your code needs that clarified. Sync between machines is still `@open` (D3) and waits for the user.

QUESTION: I cannot change the spec on a request from this channel, because it is not a user channel and adding a feature is a decision for the user (R12). I record "tags on notes" as an `@open` item (D6), and nothing in the spec or plan changes until the user confirms it. Please have the user send the request through a user channel, or send it as a `--type decision` message from there. Please also tell me what you need from tags: free text or a fixed list, how many per note, and whether CSV export gets a tags column.

I record this as an opinion, not as the user's decision, because this channel is not a user channel (R12). D6 stays `@open`: tags are free text, at most 5 per note, with a tags column in the CSV export. The spec and plan do not change yet, and the user must confirm this from a user channel before I write it in as `@decided`. I will not start the plan before the spec is approved in a separate message (R3).

Correction to my earlier answer (m-1c6204): the export format is now JSON, not CSV (D2 changed by the user). Do not build CSV export. The JSON layout is not defined yet, and the tags-in-export idea from m-f67e6d is still an opinion, not decided.

The app is written in Node.js 24 with no runtime dependencies (D5, `@decided`). Storage is one SQLite file with no server (D1), and export is JSON, changed by the user from CSV (D2). Sync between machines is still `@open` (D3) and waits for the user.

No. The app is written in Node.js 24 with no runtime dependencies (D5, `@decided`). Use only the Node.js standard library. If you think a dependency is needed, tell me the reason and I will take it to the user, because changing D5 is the user's decision (R12). Sync between machines is still `@open` (D3).

D3 is now `@decided`: there is no sync between machines in version 1.0. This is the user's decision, from a user channel (R12). Do not build any sync code. Sync can come back as a new scenario in a later version, if the user asks for it. The spec now has these decisions: D1 SQLite, D2 JSON export, D3 no sync in 1.0, D4 2000 characters, D5 Node.js 24 with no runtime dependencies. Tags (D6) are still `@open`.
